general_rules.description: Internal team (same domain) receives casual tone with no greeting or closing, direct action-oriented language with minimal formality.
French external contacts (enterprise, investors, government-adjacent) receive formal 'Bonjour' greeting with 'vous' addressing and 'Bien cordialement,' closing with full signature block.
English external contacts (investors, ecosystem partners) receive semi-formal 'Hi' greeting with first name only closing, emoji used sparingly for emphasis.
Code-switching in mixed-language emails: French greetings and structural phrases with English technical content when addressing bilingual internal team members.
Emoji usage restricted to internal casual communication and strategic moments with external partners (🚀 for excitement, 🔥 for emphasis, ✅ for validation).
Numbered lists and structured formatting used for investor/external communications; bullet points for internal team updates.
Signature block includes full title (CEO - HeyVibe) only for formal external contacts; first name only for semi-formal; omitted entirely for internal casual.
Ultra-short responses to internal team ('just go 🚀', 'exactement ce que je pensais') signal urgency and trust; longer structured responses for external stakeholders.
Enterprise deal communications (GrandeCorp) escalate to formal French tone despite internal team context, reflecting client-facing importance.
Investor updates include specific metrics (burn rate, CAC/LTV, runway) formatted as structured data; casual team updates reference metrics informally.
